children: has been selected under NASA's new Commercial Lunar Payload Services Multiple Award Contract (MAC) IDIQ — commonly referred to as CLPS 2 — officially onboarding the company into the next-generation CLPS vendor pool. The company is eligible to compete for future NASA lunar mission task orders through 2036 under a base contract ceiling of $10 billion, with an option to extend to 2041 with an increased ceiling of $15 billion.

“CLPS 2 opens a new chapter where the scope of commercial lunar missions is broader, the ambitions are larger, and the infrastructure we are building becomes even more essential,” said Dylan Taylor, Chairman and CEO, Voyager. “This selection affirms Voyager's role as a long-term partner in America's return to the Moon and its Moon Base plans.”

The CLPS 2 contract enables Voyager to bid on task orders solicited under the program, representing a significant expansion of Voyager's existing Moon Base commitment as a provider of commercial lunar services. Expanded mission types that Voyager will offer under CLPS 2 include multi-lander procurements, or "bulk buys", with metric ton landers, survive-the-night lunar surface missions, lunar sample return missions, and missions in direct support of NASA's Artemis and Moon Base Programs.
“The award is a meaningful evolution of a program that has already demonstrated what commercial lunar delivery can achieve,” said

John Thornton, executive vice president, Voyager Lunar Systems. “Our track record under CLPS 1 with four missions awarded, positions us to pursue the full spectrum of mission types this new contract will procure. CLPS 2 will deliver numerous elements of NASA’s Moon Base Program for years to come, and this award puts Voyager’s capabilities at the heart of America’s lunar future.”

The CLPS 2 selection comes as Voyager advances Griffin Mission One (Griffin-1) toward its late 2026 launch to the lunar South Pole. Griffin-1 recently completed acceptance testing and is on track to deliver the largest commercial payload in lunar history, and 10 total payloads from six countries including NASA, the European Space Agency and commercial partners.

Voyager, formerly Astrobotic, is one of the original CLPS vendors, having been onboarded to the CLPS 1 vendor pool in 2019. Under CLPS 1, the company was awarded four lunar mission contracts to date, including Griffin Mission 1 and two additional lunar lander missions in 2028. CLPS 2 is the successor to that foundational NASA initiative and is designed to extend not only its timeline and budget, but the breadth of missions it supports.

Voyager Technologies is a defense technology and space solutions company that enables mission-ready systems that secure today and power what’s next for the U.S. and partner nations. From propulsion and energetics to advanced electronics, mission management and space exploration, Voyager delivers capabilities that protect national security, reinforce the industrial base and expand human presence beyond Earth.
